You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What does an indifference curve show?

options.A: the amount of two products achievable with given income and prices
options.B: the different combinations of two goods that give a consumer equal utility
options.C: the income available to buy the two goods
options.D: the rate at which marginal utility changes as consumption changes

questions.questionText: The table shows the total amount consumers are willing to pay for different quantities of good X and the total external benefits that arise from the consumption of X. quantity of consumers’ total external good X willingness to pay benefits (000 units) ($000) ($000)
300 80 What is the value of the marginal social benefit when 5000 units are consumed?

The diagram shows the costs and revenues of a firm operating in an imperfect market. MC cost, revenue AC MR AR O W XY Z output The firm is currently producing at the profit maximising level of output. It wishes to produce at the sales maximising level of output. What would be the change in its output?

options.A: OW to OX B OW to OY C OW to OZ D OY to OZ

questions.questionText: In which market structure is dynamic efficiency least likely to occur?

options.A: oligopoly
options.B: monopolistic competition
options.C: monopoly
options.D: perfectly competitive

questions.questionText: Which type of employment contract is most likely to overcome the principal agent problem?

options.A: increasing monthly salaries of waiters in a restaurant to decrease their dependence on tips from customers
options.B: linking workers’ pay with the profits of the firm to motivate them to raise the profitability of the firm
options.C: making full fee payment in advance to a lawyer to motivate him to prepare a legal case well
options.D: offering permanent contracts to give workers job security

questions.questionText: Company R manufactures steel. Company S produces ships. Company T operates oil tankers. Company V operates cruise liners. Which statement is correct?

options.A: If R takes over S, this is an example of forwards vertical integration.
options.B: If S takes over V, this is an example of backwards vertical integration.
options.C: If T takes over S, this is an example of diversification.
options.D: If V takes over S, this is an example of horizontal integration.

questions.questionText: There are two firms in an industry. Firm X faces a choice. It can either act independently or work with its rival. If it acts independently its profit could be $900 a week but it could be only $400 a week depending on what its rival does. If it works with its rival the joint profit of the two firms together would be $1400, $700 each. It has no knowledge of what the rival’s policy will be. Which concept describes this situation?

options.A: contestable market
options.B: kinked demand curve
options.C: principal agent problem
options.D: prisoner’s dilemma

questions.questionText: A government wishes to use market forces to remove a negative externality in the consumption of a good. Which policy is likely to be the most effective?

options.A: It should provide information about the undesirable side-effects of the good.
options.B: It should give producers a subsidy, to allow consumers to purchase the product more cheaply.
options.C: It should impose an indirect tax on consumers, to reduce consumption to the socially efficient level.
options.D: It should not interfere at all, to allow the free market to generate maximum efficiency.

questions.questionText: A government decides to replace a private company with its own company to collect household waste. Why could such action be justified?

options.A: Waste collection is a public good.
options.B: Costs of waste collection are bound to be lower if paid out of local taxes.
options.C: Private companies are always less efficient than government companies.
options.D: Private companies might put profits before customer needs.

questions.questionText: What is a failure of government microeconomic intervention?

options.A: An indirect tax equal to external costs is imposed on cigarettes and the demand falls.
options.B: Limits are placed on a trade union’s restrictions that increase labour mobility.
options.C: Price controls on bread are removed which allow a free market to operate.
options.D: Tariffs are imposed on imported goods which cause the Gini coefficient to increase.

questions.questionText: What would shift the marginal revenue product curve for workers producing electric vehicles to the right?

options.A: a decrease in the price of petrol vehicles
options.B: a decrease in the productivity of electric vehicles workers
options.C: an increase in the price of electric vehicles
options.D: an increase in the wage rate of electric vehicles workers

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a perfectly competitive firm’s average product of labour (APL) and marginal product of labour (MPL) curves. wage ($), average product, marginal product (units) W APL MPL O N N N N
Which change is likely to result in a decrease in the demand for money?

options.A: a decrease in the use of credit cards by consumers
options.B: a switch from monthly to weekly payments of wages
options.C: a decrease in interest rates
options.D: an increase in the perceived risks involved in holding government bonds

questions.questionText: Which combination of factors is most likely to lead to a decrease in structural unemployment?

options.A: a fall in inflation and an increase in lending for low income households
options.B: a fall in real wages and an increase in subsidies for technological improvements
options.C: an increase in tariffs and lower taxes for new businesses
options.D: the introduction of a national minimum wage and better working conditions

questions.questionText: Why might country X have a higher natural rate of unemployment than country Y?

options.A: There is a higher level of trade unionisation in X.
options.B: There is more training and education in X.
options.C: There are greater incentives to find work in X.
options.D: There is a higher level of job vacancy information in X.

questions.questionText: Over the period of a year, nominal national income increased by 2%, inflation was 3% and population increased by 1%. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Real income decreased by 2% per head.
options.B: Real income increased by 1% per head.
options.C: Real income increased by 4% per head.
options.D: There was no change in real income per head.

questions.questionText: What is likely to be the most effective policy to reduce inflation caused by a rapid rise in import prices?

options.A: a decrease in the domestic rate of interest
options.B: a decrease in the rate of income tax
options.C: an increase in trade tariffs on imports
options.D: a revaluation of the exchange rate

questions.questionText: Which macroeconomic policy objective will not apply to a government in a closed economy?

options.A: achieving a low and steady rate of inflation
options.B: achieving a more equal income distribution
options.C: achieving a surplus on the balance of payments
options.D: achieving a sustainable rate of economic growth

questions.questionText: A government increases its budget deficit to spend money on infrastructure development. It finances this by printing money. How is this policy likely to affect the government’s main macroeconomic policy objectives? higher lower lower economic unemployment inflation growth

options.A: less likely less likely more likely
options.B: less likely more likely less likely
options.C: more likely more likely less likely
options.D: more likely more likely more likely

questions.questionText: The government increases interest rates in order to reduce the rate of inflation. What will also result from this action?

options.A: a depreciation of the country’s currency
options.B: a fall in the level of savings
options.C: a reduction in economic growth
options.D: a reduction in unemployment

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between the income tax rate and tax revenue. tax X revenue W O Z Y income tax rate Which statement is correct?

options.A: A tax rate cut from Y to Z will cause tax revenue to decrease.
options.B: At tax rates below Z a tax rate cut will cause tax revenue to increase.
options.C: The greater the rate of tax beyond Z, the smaller will be the tax revenue generated.
options.D: Tax revenue will always increase as the rate of income tax increases.

questions.questionText: In which situation is devaluation of the currency most likely to cause inflation?

options.A: Excess capacity is available.
options.B: Import tariffs are reduced.
options.C: Local substitutes of imported raw materials are unavailable.
options.D: The demand for exports is price inelastic.

questions.questionText: A country imports most of the raw materials used as factor inputs. Which policy is most likely to control cost-push inflation?

options.A: an appreciation of the exchange rate
options.B: an increase in the rate of income tax
options.C: an increase in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase in the rate of sales tax

questions.questionText: Germany, one of the world’s strongest trading nations, achieved a surplus on current account of the balance of payments in 2021–2022. Which income flow would not have been included in the calculation of Germany’s current account?

options.A: Declining sales of German cars for export overseas.
options.B: Falling earnings of foreign exchange from visitors to Germany.
options.C: Increasing transfers of aid to less developed countries.
options.D: Investment in a natural gas pipeline link to its main foreign supplier.

questions.questionText: A country maintains its foreign exchange rate against the United States dollar, within a narrow but changing band. What is this type of exchange rate?

options.A: fixed
options.B: floating
options.C: managed float
options.D: trade-weighted

In a period, the distribution of income becomes more unequal but the distribution of wealth becomes more equal. Which movement would show the effects of these changes on the distribution of income and wealth within the country? distribution of income distribution of wealth

questions.questionText: What is likely to happen in a developing country as it becomes more developed?

options.A: A lower percentage of people will go to university.
options.B: Average life expectancy will rise.
options.C: The rate of population growth will increase.
